messages:
marta: Heads up — Acme reported a big jump in tail latency (p95/p99) for text-generation last hour, went from ~120ms p95 to ~420ms. They opened a support ticket: https://support/acme/INC-9823 :exclamation:
jon: saw that. Our hosted dashboard also shows a p99 spike around 2024-05-05T14:02Z. But the raw histogram doesn't look as bad. p95 vs histogram disagreeing.
elia: can you paste the dashboard query? maybe it's using a 5m rollup that includes a noisy outlier bucket.
marta: panel uses `latency_ms` quantile(0.95) from `ingress.requests` with `agg=rollup(1m)` in grafana. hist view is the prometheus histogram for `ingress_request_duration_seconds_bucket` converted to ms.
jon: aha — rollup(1m) vs raw histogram buckets can diverge when a few long requests fall at edges. Also our quantile rollup uses the TDigest aggregator which can skew for small sample counts.
tariq: @marta can you confirm whether Acme was on the new routing policy (zone-prefer) at the time? we rolled that yesterday.
marta: checking ticket logs — they were routed via us-west-2 primary, no zone-prefer flag.
sre-bot: deploy-bot: deployment 2024-05-05T13:40Z rolled: inference-runtime v2.6.1 -> v2.6.2 (canary 10%). No rollbacks.
elia: could the new runtime change kernel scheduling that affects tail latency? we did change async worker pool sizing.
jon: we need to reproduce. Steps to collect: 1) run synth load hitting same model/version, 2) capture headers X-Instance, X-KV-Cache-hit, 3) enable debug trace on one request. I'll open an internal repro run.
marta: in support ticket they included a curl that shows slow streaming start (first byte delayed). Looks like stall before token generation.
tariq: that suggests scheduling backpressure (worker busy) or long disk I/O for KV cache load. Was there any OOM/killed pods?
jon: k8s events around 13:35-14:10 show 4 pod restarts on inf-pool-usw2-01 due to liveness probe failures. Logs show `OOMKilled` on pid 2074.
elia: OOMs explain stalls. Why would v2.6.2 use more memory? we changed kv-cache prefetch size config in that release.
marta: support notes that affected requests were larger context (>=8k tokens). Prefetch could spike memory on big contexts.
support-bot: ticket INC-9823 updated: customer confirmed observed pattern matches times of our deploy.
jon: mitigation: revert scaling config or increase pod memory on canary pods. Short-term: roll back v2.6.2 canary (10% -> 0) and promote v2.6.1 for production until fix.
tariq: also patch dashboards to show both `quantile(0.95)` from rollup and computed p95 from raw histogram side-by-side to avoid future confusion.
elia: agree. I'll file a tiny PR to add raw-hist p95 panel and annotate deploy time.
marta: I'll propose the rollback to ops and update the customer.
jon: for postmortem, we should capture: reproduce script, list of pod events, JVM/py process memory profiles, and propose config change (cap prefetch or stream kv on demand).
sre-bot: action created: SRE-847 add raw-hist p95 panel and annotate deploys. Assigned to elia.
marta: customer update posted. They're asking for ETA — suggest 30–60m after rollback. They asked for token-level logs for 3 sample request ids — I'll request them.
tariq: FYI: if we roll back, we need to ensure no partial canary traffic stays on v2.6.2. I'll watch routing tables.
jon: repro command I'm running (internal):
```
ab -n 2000 -c 20 -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEST_KEY" \
  -p generate_payload.json https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate?model=redwood-3b
```
elia: added dashboard PR: https://git/repo/patch/1234 — includes annotation layer and raw hist panel.
marta: status update: ops approved rollback. rolling canary down now.
sre-bot: deploy-bot: canary scale set to 0% for inference-runtime v2.6.2 at 2024-05-05T14:15Z.
jon: monitoring p95/p99 now — initial 15m after rollback looks back to baseline. will keep watching for 1h.
marta: thanks team. We'll close ticket after 2h stable and send postmortem with mitigation plan. :thumbsup:
